chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Ja'far ibn Hayyan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who dedicated the yield of his property to a relative of his father and a relative of his mother, and bequeathed to a man and his offspring from that yield, with no kinship between him and the beneficiary, [the amount of] three hundred dirhams every year, and the remainder was to be distributed among his relatives from his father and his relatives from his mother. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is permissible for the one to whom it was bequeathed to receive that.'

I said: 'What is your view if the yield from the land that was dedicated does not exceed five hundred dirhams?' He said: 'Is it not in his bequest that the beneficiary should be given three hundred dirhams from the yield, and the remainder distributed among his relatives from his mother and his relatives from his father?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'His relatives cannot take anything from the yield until the beneficiary is paid three hundred dirhams; then for them is what remains after that.'

I said: 'What is your view if the beneficiary dies?' He said: 'If he dies, the three hundred dirhams belong to his heirs, who inherit it as long as one of them remains. When his heirs are cut off and no one remains from among them, the three hundred dirhams [return] to the relatives of the deceased, to be returned to what comes out of the endowment, then it is distributed among them; they inherit that as long as they remain, and the yield continues.'

I said: 'So for the heirs from the relatives of the deceased is that they can sell the land if they need to, and what comes out of the yield does not suffice for them.' He said: 'Yes, when all of them agree and the sale is better for them, they sell.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for distributing yield from an endowment when a fixed amount is bequeathed to a non-relative?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the precedence of fixed annual bequests over residual inheritance within a waqf, emphasizing the priority of the designated beneficiary's share before relatives receive the remainder. It further details the hereditary nature of this fixed stipend upon the beneficiary's death and establishes the condition of mutual consent for selling the endowed property if the yield proves insufficient. This ruling highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in balancing charitable endowments with familial financial needs.
